text:
Shane Pinto is having the kind of season that makes a second-round pick look like a bargain. He has ten goals and 18 points in 25 games at 20:08 a night, a top-line workload, and his winner against Calgary pushed Ottawa's point streak to nine. He ranks 19th in the league in wins added by goals.

The finishing looks honest: ten goals on 9.2 expected, because he keeps shooting from dangerous spots. He's also physical (42 hits, 20 blocks), and the Senators lean on him in hard minutes. The one soft number is relative: Ottawa's share of expected goals is 5.9 points worse with him on the ice than off, though still above even at 51%. That's often the price of tough matchups. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) finds no clear strength or weakness yet. Our numbers say he plays like Tom Wilson. Our range projects 50 to 71 points and 23 to 36 goals.
